metadata.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
metadata.authors: Ben Mildenhall, Pratul P. Srinivasan, Matthew Tancik, Jonathan T. Barron, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Ren Ng

nodes.name: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)
nodes.statement: A continuous 5D vector-valued function $F_\Theta : (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\mathbf{c}, \sigma)$ approximated by an MLP, mapping 3D location $\mathbf{x}=(x,y,z)$ and 2D viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$ to emitted RGB color $\mathbf{c}$ and volume density $\sigma$.
nodes.statement_clean: A 5D continuous scene function (location + viewing direction to color + density) parameterized by an MLP.

nodes.name: Volume density
nodes.statement: $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ is the differential probability of a ray terminating at an infinitesimal particle at location $\mathbf{x}$.

nodes.name: Accumulated transmittance
nodes.statement: $T(t) = \exp\left(-\int_{t_n}^{t} \sigma(\mathbf{r}(s))\,ds\right)$ denotes the probability that the ray travels from $t_n$ to $t$ without hitting any other particle.

nodes.name: Camera ray
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ with origin $\mathbf{o}$, direction $\mathbf{d}$, and near/far bounds $t_n, t_f$.

nodes.name: Positional encoding
nodes.statement: Mapping $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{2L}$ defined by $\gamma(p) = (\sin(2^0 \pi p), \cos(2^0 \pi p), \ldots, \sin(2^{L-1} \pi p), \cos(2^{L-1} \pi p))$, applied separately to each coordinate of $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A sinusoidal embedding lifting each scalar coordinate into a $2L$-dimensional Fourier-feature vector.

nodes.name: Stratified sampling for ray integration
nodes.statement: Partition $[t_n, t_f]$ into $N$ evenly-spaced bins and draw $t_i \sim \mathcal{U}[t_n + \frac{i-1}{N}(t_f-t_n),\, t_n + \frac{i}{N}(t_f-t_n)]$ for $i=1,\ldots,N$.

nodes.name: Normalized device coordinates (NDC) space
nodes.statement: Space obtained by the standard 3D perspective projection that maps the original viewing frustum to the cube $[-1,1]^3$ and converts the camera $z$-axis to be linear in disparity (inverse depth).

nodes.name: Continuous volume rendering integral
nodes.statement: $C(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{t_n}^{t_f} T(t)\,\sigma(\mathbf{r}(t))\,\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r}(t),\mathbf{d})\,dt$, where $T(t) = \exp(-\int_{t_n}^{t}\sigma(\mathbf{r}(s))\,ds)$.

nodes.name: Quadrature estimator of ray color
nodes.statement: $\hat{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i\,(1-\exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))\,\mathbf{c}_i$, where $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ and $\delta_i = t_{i+1}-t_i$.
nodes.origin_citation: Max 1995, Optical models for direct volume rendering

nodes.name: Coarse-network weight formula
nodes.statement: $\hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N_c} w_i c_i$ with $w_i = T_i(1-\exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))$; normalized weights $\hat{w}_i = w_i / \sum_{j=1}^{N_c} w_j$ define a piecewise-constant PDF along the ray.

nodes.name: NeRF training loss
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L} = \sum_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{R}} \left[\,\lVert \hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r}) - C(\mathbf{r}) \rVert_2^2 + \lVert \hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r}) - C(\mathbf{r}) \rVert_2^2\,\right]$ over a minibatch $\mathcal{R}$ of camera rays.

nodes.name: NDC-space ray origin and direction
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{o}' = (-\frac{f_{cam}}{W/2}\frac{o_x}{o_z},\, -\frac{f_{cam}}{H/2}\frac{o_y}{o_z},\, 1+\frac{2n}{o_z})$ and $\mathbf{d}' = (-\frac{f_{cam}}{W/2}(\frac{d_x}{d_z}-\frac{o_x}{o_z}),\, -\frac{f_{cam}}{H/2}(\frac{d_y}{d_z}-\frac{o_y}{o_z}),\, -\frac{2n}{o_z})$ for the far plane at infinity.

nodes.name: Novel view synthesis from sparse RGB images
nodes.statement: Given a set of input RGB images of a scene with known camera poses, synthesize photorealistic novel views from previously unseen viewpoints.
nodes.statement_clean: Synthesize new views of a scene from a sparse set of posed RGB images.

nodes.name: NeRF rendering and optimization
nodes.statement: Optimize an MLP $F_\Theta$ representing a 5D radiance field by rendering rays via stratified + hierarchical sampling and minimizing photometric loss between rendered and observed pixels.
input: RGB images of a scene with known camera poses and intrinsics
Scene bounds $t_n, t_f$ (or NDC mapping for forward-facing scenes)
MLP architecture $F_\Theta$ (8 layers, 256 channels for $\mathbf{x}$ branch; 1 layer, 128 channels for $\mathbf{d}$ branch)
Number of coarse and fine samples $N_c, N_f$ per ray
output: Trained MLP weights $\Theta$ that encode the scene as a continuous neural radiance field
Rendered novel-view images $\hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r})$ for any specified camera

nodes.name: Hierarchical volume sampling
nodes.statement: Two-pass sampling: a coarse network is evaluated at $N_c$ stratified samples, then a fine network is evaluated at the union of those samples and $N_f$ additional samples drawn via inverse-CDF sampling from the coarse network's normalized weights.
input: Camera ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ with bounds $t_n, t_f$
output: Fine rendered color $\hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r})$ using all $N_c+N_f$ samples

nodes.name: Realistic Synthetic 360 dataset
nodes.statement: Pathtraced 800x800 renderings of 8 objects with complex geometry and non-Lambertian materials (chair, drums, ficus, hotdog, lego, materials, mic, ship), with 100 input views and 200 test views per scene.

nodes.name: Diffuse Synthetic 360 dataset
nodes.statement: DeepVoxels dataset: four Lambertian objects with simple geometry, rendered at 512x512 from 479 input and 1000 test viewpoints on the upper hemisphere.

nodes.name: Real Forward-Facing dataset
nodes.statement: Eight real-world scenes captured with a handheld cellphone (5 from LLFF, 3 new), 20-62 images each at 1008x756 pixels, with $\nicefrac{1}{8}$ held out for testing.

nodes.name: Ablation study on Realistic Synthetic 360
nodes.statement: Removing positional encoding, view-dependence, or hierarchical sampling each individually degrades quality; positional encoding and view-dependence give the largest gains; performance saturates around $L=10$ for $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$.

nodes.name: Neural Volumes (NV)
nodes.statement: Optimizes a deep 3D convolutional network to predict a discretized $128^3$ RGB$\alpha$ voxel grid plus a $32^3$ warp grid, rendering by marching camera rays through the warped voxel grid.

nodes.name: Scene Representation Networks (SRN)
nodes.statement: Represents a scene as an opaque surface defined by an MLP from $(x,y,z)$ to a feature vector; a recurrent neural network marches along each ray and the final feature is decoded into a single color.
nodes.origin_citation: Sitzmann et al., Scene Representation Networks (NeurIPS 2019)

nodes.name: Local Light Field Fusion (LLFF)
nodes.statement: A trained 3D CNN predicts per-view discretized frustum-sampled RGB$\alpha$ multiplane images (MPIs); novel views are rendered by alpha-compositing and blending nearby MPIs.

nodes.name: Differentiability of the alpha-compositing renderer
nodes.statement: The quadrature estimator $\hat{C}(\mathbf{r})$ is trivially differentiable in $(\mathbf{c}_i, \sigma_i)$ and reduces to traditional alpha compositing with $\alpha_i = 1-\exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$.

nodes.name: Multiview consistency via $\sigma$ as function of $\mathbf{x}$ alone
nodes.statement: Restricting the volume density $\sigma$ to depend only on location $\mathbf{x}$ (while letting RGB depend on both $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$) enforces multiview-consistent geometry and lets the model represent non-Lambertian view-dependent appearance.

nodes.name: Implementation hyperparameters
nodes.statement: Batch of 4096 rays, $N_c=64$ coarse and $N_f=128$ fine samples per ray, Adam with learning rate decaying from $5\times 10^{-4}$ to $5\times 10^{-5}$; 100k-300k iterations on a single NVIDIA V100 (1-2 days).

nodes.name: Why Fourier features help
nodes.statement: Deep MLPs are biased towards low-frequency functions (Rahaman et al. 2018); mapping inputs through high-frequency sinusoids before the MLP enables fitting high-frequency variation in color and geometry.

nodes.name: NDC ray-space transformation preserves projected ray geometry
nodes.statement: For a ray $\mathbf{o}+t\mathbf{d}$ in camera space, the NDC ray $\mathbf{o}'+t'\mathbf{d}'$ defined by the perspective-projection formulas above satisfies $\pi(\mathbf{o}+t\mathbf{d}) = \mathbf{o}'+t'\mathbf{d}'$ for all $t \geq 0$, with $t'=0 \Leftrightarrow t=0$ and $t' \to 1$ as $t \to \infty$.
assumptions: Pinhole camera with focal length $f_{cam}$, image dimensions $W \times H$, near plane $n$, far plane $f$
conclusions: The map sends camera rays to NDC-space rays that trace the same projected points
Sampling $t' \in [0,1]$ linearly yields linear sampling in disparity from $n$ to $\infty$ in the original space

nodes.name: Derivation of NDC ray-space transformation
nodes.statement: Project the standard perspective matrix, equate components of $\pi(\mathbf{o}+t\mathbf{d})$ with $\mathbf{o}'+t'\mathbf{d}'$, fix the gauge $t=0 \Leftrightarrow t'=0$, and factor out a common $t$-dependent expression to read off $\mathbf{o}', \mathbf{d}', t'$.

nodes.name: Write the perspective projection in homogeneous form
nodes.statement: Write the perspective matrix $M$ with entries $\frac{n}{r}, \frac{n}{t}, \frac{-(f+n)}{f-n}, \frac{-2fn}{f-n}, -1$ acting on $(x,y,z,1)^\top$, then divide by the fourth coordinate to obtain $\pi(x,y,z) = (a_x x/z, a_y y/z, a_z + b_z/z)$.

nodes.name: Match origin via the gauge $t=t'=0$
nodes.statement: Substituting $t=0,\,t'=0$ into the equality $\pi(\mathbf{o}+t\mathbf{d}) = \mathbf{o}'+t'\mathbf{d}'$ yields $\mathbf{o}' = \pi(\mathbf{o}) = (a_x o_x/o_z,\, a_y o_y/o_z,\, a_z + b_z/o_z)$.

nodes.name: Solve for direction and reparameterize $t'$
nodes.statement: Subtracting $\mathbf{o}'$ from both sides and simplifying gives $t'\mathbf{d}'$ as a common factor $\frac{t d_z}{o_z + t d_z}$ times direction-only entries; defining $t' = \frac{t d_z}{o_z + t d_z}$ reads off $\mathbf{d}'$ with the components $a_x(d_x/d_z - o_x/o_z)$, $a_y(d_y/d_z - o_y/o_z)$, $-b_z/o_z$.

nodes.name: Specialize to $f \to \infty$ and pinhole camera
nodes.statement: Letting $f \to \infty$ gives $a_z = 1, b_z = 2n$; and using $a_x = -f_{cam}/(W/2),\, a_y = -f_{cam}/(H/2)$ from the pinhole camera yields the final NDC ray formulas in Eq. EP226.5.

nodes.name: Initialize MLP weights and sample a ray batch
nodes.statement: Initialize the coarse and fine MLP weights $\Theta_c, \Theta_f$; at each iteration sample a batch $\mathcal{R}$ of 4096 camera rays uniformly across all training pixels.

nodes.name: Positional-encode coordinates
nodes.statement: For each sampled 5D coordinate $(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{d})$, apply $\gamma(\cdot)$ component-wise with $L=10$ for $\mathbf{x}$ and $L=4$ for $\mathbf{d}$.

nodes.name: Hierarchical sampling and forward pass
nodes.statement: Run AP226.2 to obtain $N_c$ coarse and $N_c+N_f$ fine 3D query points along each ray; query $F_\Theta^{c}, F_\Theta^{f}$ to get $(\mathbf{c}_i, \sigma_i)$; alpha-composite via Eq. EP226.2 to obtain $\hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r}), \hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r})$.

nodes.name: Compute loss and gradient step
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathcal{L} = \sum_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{R}}[\lVert\hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r})-C(\mathbf{r})\rVert_2^2 + \lVert\hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r})-C(\mathbf{r})\rVert_2^2]$ and update $\Theta_c,\Theta_f$ via Adam with learning rate decaying from $5\times 10^{-4}$ to $5\times 10^{-5}$.

nodes.name: Iterate until convergence
nodes.statement: Repeat steps 1-4 for 100k-300k iterations on a single NVIDIA V100; return trained weights $\Theta_c,\Theta_f$ and use the fine network to render novel views.

nodes.name: Coarse stratified sampling
nodes.statement: Draw $N_c$ coarse sample positions $\{t_i\}_{i=1}^{N_c}$ along the ray via stratified sampling on $[t_n, t_f]$ (Eq. EP226.6 / DP226.6).

nodes.name: Evaluate coarse network and rendered color
nodes.statement: Query coarse network $F_\Theta^{c}$ at each of the $N_c$ samples; compute $\hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_i w_i c_i$ with $w_i = T_i(1-\exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))$ (Eq. EP226.3).

nodes.name: Inverse-CDF importance sampling for fine network
nodes.statement: Normalize weights $\hat{w}_i = w_i / \sum_j w_j$ to obtain a piecewise-constant PDF, then draw $N_f$ additional samples via inverse transform sampling on this PDF.

nodes.name: Evaluate fine network on the union of samples
nodes.statement: Query fine network $F_\Theta^{f}$ at the $N_c + N_f$ pooled samples and compute $\hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r})$ via the quadrature rule (Eq. EP226.2).
